verdicts.evidence: Tile: 'Pick any two pieces and see what they share, where they split, and the question nobody has answered yet.' Home: 'Some pairings are documented. Most are open.' The script holds 9 written pairings (w(...) x9) against 109 pages in connections.json; any other pair returns 'An open pairing. No documented connection yet... a resemblance, not a finding.' with no share/split/question. 'Includes the state lens' is supported (twenty states).
verdicts.fix: Pick any two pieces. Nine pairings are written up: what they share, where they split, and a question nobody has answered yet. The rest are open for you to find. Includes the state lens.

verdicts.evidence: Tile: 'One composite person, twelve files.' Home never says twelve. Its ledger has 11 life stages and 13 file entries (the last stage opens three). The counter reaches 13 with both apps taken, 12 with one skipped, 11 with both skipped. 'Composite' and the two counts (alarms for the institution, laws for the person) are supported.
verdicts.fix: One composite person, up to thirteen files. Count the alarms that protect the institution and the laws that protect the person.

verdicts.evidence: Home: five switches (stolen card, scam, gambling habit, power plant overrun, data center's power); 'test that across five kinds of loss'; lamp shows whether an alarm got built; 'If a switch seems to break the thesis, flag it.' Tile names four of the five and says 'five losses'.
Home: 'Ten clocks from across the site. Pick two.'; array C has 10 rows, shortest '2 days' (Regulation E, 2 business days), longest '463 years'; 'Tap any two clocks to race them.'

Home Room 1: 'One fact about you. Five different prices.' The five cards are Sportsbook, Church outreach (a consultant to nonprofits), Sorting engine, Reputation market, Companion app. Tile matches and names no company.

Home: 'Here are five current apps and one benchmark from 2000'; 'what does its privacy policy say happens to your data if the company is sold or fails?'; 'Audit any app in one minute.' Note: home says the wording is 'as captured by policy trackers and news reports. We did not read the live policies directly'; the tile's 'what five apps say' drops that, as does the home page's own heading.
Home: 'follow that one message backward: through the chips, the building, the loan, the grid and the bill.' Stops: You, Chips, Building, Loan, Grid, Bill.

Tile: 'Britain made banks repay scam victims, and scam losses fell.' Home: 'British banks must repay most victims of these scams' [REPORTED]; 54% -> 65% of all claims reimbursed, 97% of in-scope claims; cap of GBP 85,000 and a gross-negligence exception. The fall is one review's finding: 'An independent review found ... scam losses fell by about GBP 73 million a year' [REPORTED], and home lists as WATCH 'How much of Britain's drop in losses would have happened anyway; the review attributes it to the policy, using its own method.' Tile drops 'most' and states the review's attributed finding as settled, untagged. 'In the US, the customer usually pays' matches home ('in the United States you usually lose it all'; 'banks are generally not required to repay you'). The three interactions (text, vault dials, border) exist in Rooms 1 to 3.
verdicts.fix: Britain made banks repay most scam victims, and an independent review found scam losses fell by about GBP 73 million a year. In the US, the customer usually pays. Answer the text, press the vault dials, cross the border.
